id.description: Stable identifier. Lowercase country prefix, underscore, slug.

language.description: ISO 639-1 where one exists, otherwise ISO 639-3

news_sitemaps.description: Google News sitemaps (or sitemap indexes) the site lists in robots.txt, polled as editorial feeds beside the RSS feeds, never in their place. A news sitemap lists every article of the last two days with its title and publication date, so a busy site whose short RSS feed overflows between polls loses nothing. Items go through the keyword gate on the title alone. See pipeline/news_sitemap.py.

network.description: The media group the outlet belongs to (acm, news_corp, nine, postmedia, torstar, ...), set where the notes or the ownership source name the group. Outlets of one network share a newsroom system or copy pool, so an earlier copy at a sister outlet is never taken as the original of a copy (pipeline/copies.py). Unset means no group is recorded.

junk_feed.description: A feed of the outlet that stopped carrying its news (hijacked, or turned to gambling, advertorial or placeholder posts). Every stored item from it with a day of record on or after since is withdrawn by pipeline/junk_feeds.py: its labels are marked not current, its status becomes junk_feed, and its discovery is taken off the per day counts. From since to the day before until (for good when until is unset) the feed was the outlet's only feed, so the outlet's whole discovery on those days is withdrawn; on and after until only the feed's own stored items are. An active outlet needs until and must no longer poll the feed.

since.description: First day of record on which the feed's items were not the outlet's news, read from the stored titles.

until.description: Day the outlet stopped polling the feed, when it went on with another feed.

audience_rank.description: Rank of the outlet by audience within its country, 1 = largest. Set from a readership source; unset means unknown. The share of all published items metric uses the 30 best ranked outlets of a country when ranks exist, otherwise every active outlet.

collector.description: Which collector polls this outlet. hosted (default) is the GitHub-hosted runner; self_hosted was the relay on the owner's own network, for feeds that refuse GitHub's addresses, retired on 2026-10-22, so every self_hosted outlet is inactive; both puts a short feed the hosted runner reaches too rarely on both schedules, and its article pages are fetched by the hosted runner only.

collector_since.description: Day the outlet came onto its current collector, or was reactivated on it. The weekly feed validation (pipeline/validate_sources.py) counts an outlet's silence from this day at the earliest, so failures recorded before a move to the relay or a reactivation never deactivate it.

section_feeds.description: Press release, sponsored and partner sections that editorial RSS usually leaves out, found by pipeline/discover_sections.py. type rss is a feed; type page is the section's index page, read for article links. Items from these sections skip the relevance gate; classification decides.

type.description: rss: a feed. page: a section index page whose article links are read like feed entries. aap_widget: a page filled by the AAP release widget, read from the AAP release listing (pipeline/section_pages.py).

release_sections.description: Whether the outlet's site was searched for press release, sponsored or partner sections, when, and what was found. Unsearched outlets have no entry. The flag is a finding: state origin can only be found where the route was looked for.

readable.description: Whether the collector could read the section when last verified. Unreadable sections stay recorded but are not polled.

rejected.description: true when the page is not a section of this kind (a desk, a topic page, a single story). Discovery never registers it again, as a page or a feed, however often a probe finds it.

rejected_feed.description: A feed once registered for this section and removed because it is not the section's feed (often the site-wide feed). Discovery never registers it again for any of the outlet's sections, and the section is registered again only on another feed. pipeline/section_retag.py reads it to correct the items that feed brought in.

rejected_feed_language.description: Language of the rejected feed's items when it is not the outlet's, so the correction gates them in the right language.

reason.description: Why the section or its feed was rejected.

political_leaning.description: Editorial leaning judged against the outlet's own country's political spectrum, not a US or European one. state_controlled when the outlet is state owned without editorial independence (ownership: state), so its line is the government's rather than a left or right one; the source is the ownership source. unassessed when no reliable source was found; never inferred from the name, language or country.

leaning_source.description: URL of the source for political_leaning. Media Bias/Fact Check rates outlets on a United States spectrum; where it is the only source for an outlet outside the United States, the export marks the leaning leaning_source_weak and the site shows it with a caution.

leaning_second_source.description: URL of a second, independent source that agrees with political_leaning. A second source that is not Media Bias/Fact Check lifts the weak mark from a Media Bias/Fact Check leaning outside the United States.

ownership.description: private; public_service, a domestic public broadcaster with statutory editorial independence; state_funded_international, a broadcaster funded by a government to reach audiences abroad, whose editorial independence rests on a statute, charter or grant agreement (Radio Free Asia, RFE/RL, Voice of America, Deutsche Welle, RFI, France 24, BBC World Service language services, KBS World), kept apart from domestic public service because its funder's foreign policy is its remit; state, government controlled or state owned without editorial independence, at home or abroad (RT, Sputnik, CGTN); party, owned by a political party; unassessed.

ownership_source.description: URL of the source for ownership.

government_stance.description: Stance toward the government of the outlet's own country, from a dated third-party source (RSF, Freedom House, the Media Ownership Monitor, Media Landscapes, BBC media guides). state_controlled is derived from a sourced state ownership. An outlet's description of itself does not count; unassessed when no dated source describes it.

stance_source.description: URL of the source for government_stance.

stance_as_of.description: The year the stance source describes. A stance is toward the government of the day, so a source older than a change of government is not used.

rank_source.description: URL of the readership source behind audience_rank.
